title: Decentralized Dead Drop — blue and grey icon concepts

selection.name: Sealed conversation
selection.decision: User selected the letter combined with the chat bubble for the real application.

concepts.name: Folded drop
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Create ONE polished app icon concept for "Decentralized Dead Drop", an independent private messaging app where communities operate their own delivery server. This is an original brand exploration. Deliver a single isolated square app icon, not a website, presentation sheet, wordmark or device mockup.
Visual style: precise minimal geometric identity, strong silhouette, flat vector-style graphic with smooth edges, carefully balanced proportions and broad confident shapes. Designed to stay intelligible at small sizes. Use exclusively deep cobalt blue #264A9A, cool light grey #E9EDF4, pale blue #DBE4F8, slate grey #68758A, and tiny amounts of white where needed. No other hues, no gradient, bevel, glow, cast shadow, photorealism, glass, texture, 3D extrusion or hairline strokes. Avoid padlocks, shields, checkmarks, cryptocurrency symbols and connected-node meshes. Communicate private messages and independent delivery using simple visual metaphor.
Canvas: 1024 by 1024. A single cool-light-grey rounded-square app tile centered on a genuinely transparent outer canvas, generous transparent margin of about 9 percent. The tile is approximately 82 percent of canvas width with a modern corner radius. The central symbol occupies about 60 percent of tile width, with ample safe area around it. Tile is perfectly straight-on and square, not tilted or in perspective. No lettering, typography, labels or watermarks except where a geometric monogram is specifically requested. The shape must look carefully designed, not like generic clip art. Keep the interior tile background fully opaque; only the region outside the tile is transparent.

Concept: a sealed envelope condensed into a distinctive compact hexagonal drop-box silhouette. Build one cobalt-blue upright geometric hexagonal body, about equally tall as wide, with slightly softened corner transitions. A clean broad pale-grey negative-space V-shaped fold crosses its upper third, so the same symbol reads as a sealed message and the closed lid of a small dead-drop box. A subtle single slate-grey upper facet gives the fold clarity without making it 3D. No literal water droplet, no lock, no tiny seal or extra adornment. Prioritize an elegant, unmistakable silhouette.

Concept: the moment a sealed message is deposited into a private dead drop. One compact cobalt-blue letterbox shape occupies the lower center of the icon, with generous rounded outer corners and one wide horizontal light-grey mail slot in its upper part. A single light-grey rectangular envelope, edged in cobalt and with a bold blue V-shaped flap, enters that slot from above at a small intentional 12-degree diagonal. The lower portion of the envelope is cleanly occluded by the box; the slot and overlap must be unambiguous. Use very few shapes, make both the envelope and box large and readable. No postbox stand, antenna, latch, arrows, screws, labels, server LEDs or decorative details. A simple dignified mark, visually balanced.

Concept: an original abstract DD monogram suggesting two independent endpoints exchanging a private message. Construct two sturdy geometric uppercase D forms, one cobalt blue and one slate grey. The blue D is the left foreground shape; the slate D is the right rear shape. Overlap them with a broad clean light-grey negative-space separation so each D remains recognizable and the combined silhouette is compact and balanced. Both D counters are open and large. Use semicircular curves, straight vertical spines, and consistent broad weight. No interlaced rings, chain-link shapes or arrows. This is the only permitted lettering: the two D letters are custom geometric symbol forms, not typed text. No letter E, no full product name, no additional characters. Crisp typographic craftsmanship and memorable geometry.

Concept: a message envelope and a conversation bubble fused into one symbol. A single large cobalt-blue rounded rectangular chat bubble, with a short integrated tail at its lower left. Across the upper half of this filled bubble, a broad light-grey negative-space V suggests the flap of a sealed envelope. Behind it, a small offset slate-grey bubble is visible only as a restrained upper-right outline and a tiny right-side tail; it indicates another person without making the composition busy. Two clean bold forms, wide negative-space separation, and no tiny details. Do not include three dots, a lock, checkmarks or notification badges. The front bubble must simultaneously read as an envelope and conversation.
